items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode A (Objective Evaluation), the report implements a methodologically sound DIDS-MFL pipeline and episodic few-shot benchmark against ~12 baselines on NF-UNSW-NB15-v2 (the single dataset provided), reporting both F1 and NMI across 5 seeds. However, the quantitative metrics fall notably short of the original paper's 96.00% ± 1.12 F1 and 92.04% ± 1.36 NMI: DIDS-MFL achieves 71.3% ± 4.2 F1 and 56.2% NMI at 4-way 5-shot with its native bi-similarity head (reaching 80.3% ± 1.1 F1 / 64.6% NMI at 5-shot and 85.0% F1 / 70.1% NMI at 10-shot only with a post-hoc logistic-regression head). Consequently, it does not reproduce the paper's 71.91%–125.19% F1 and 71.95%–144.07% NMI relative gains, low variance over 10 runs, or consistent superiority across all tasks and baselines (trailing support-set RF and fine-tuned MLP at K>=5 under its own head, as well as RF on known-attack typing).

items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode A (Objective), the report directly implements a 100-flow accuracy and latency benchmark (Section 5.7, Tables 6–6b), where DIDS-MFL achieves 1.00 binary F1 (99.1% on the full test set, comparable to the paper's 99.52%) and 0.68 10-class macro-F1 at 0.302 ms/flow (~0.03s per 100 flows, faster than the paper's 6.41s), while adding a rigorous 20-shot Random Forest control and practical deployability analysis. However, due to environment constraints, the agent evaluated Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on fp32 CPU (0.82 binary F1, 0.20 macro-F1, 3.25s/flow) rather than GPT-3.5/4, making the LLM accuracy and latency baseline substantially weaker than the frontier models in Table VIII, alongside a modest 8-epoch multi-class F1 for DIDS-MFL. Overall, the metrics and deployability findings are roughly comparable to the original paper with transparent caveats, warranting a score of 45.
